beats.care: Next time you or a parent gets treated, ask for an itemised bill. You can compare what the hospital paid with what you paid.
beats.what: A state drugs regulator circular says bills must list purchase cost, MRP and the price charged for medicines, implants and consumables.
beats.why: The regulator said patients are billed near MRP "without any transparency". It wants patients to see the gap.

cards.body: Applies to government, private and trust hospitals, clinics, nursing homes and diagnostic centres.
cards.caption: Start date

cards.body: Each line must show the generic and brand name, batch number, expiry date, MRP, price charged and taxes. The price charged can't cross MRP.
The rule covers outpatient visits too, not just hospital stays.

cards.q: Do you check medicine prices on bills?

opts: What the hospital paid to buy each item
cards.q: What new detail must Karnataka hospital bills show?
cards.why: Bills must now list the procurement cost alongside MRP and the price the patient pays.

hook: Ever wondered what a hospital *actually paid* for your medicine?

learn.t: State drug inspectors flagged pricing concerns on 253 medicines and consumables before this order, South First reports.

sources.name: South First
sources.title: What hospitals pay versus what patients pay: Karnataka orders disclosure of medicine costs on bills

tldr: From November 1, Karnataka hospitals must show what they paid for medicines and supplies on every patient's bill.
watch: New-format itemised bills become mandatory in all Karnataka hospitals and clinics from November 1, 2026.
